title: Work backward from a mean to a missing value
subtitle: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread · 10 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **10 of the official questions in One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread are this one** — 1 Easy, 1 Medium, 8 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- One data value is an unknown (x, or 'the value not shown'), and you are told the mean, or that two sets' means are equal or differ by a set amount.
- Or two groups' means and sizes are given and you need the combined mean.
- Hard versions add median and range conditions on an ordered list with several constants.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Convert each mean to a total: sum = mean × count.
- 2) Set up the equation (known sum + x = required total) and solve.
- For combined groups, add the two totals and divide by the combined count; do not average the two means.
- 3) With median or range conditions, use position (middle term) and max − min to pin down constants first.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the equation, e.g. (a+b+c+d+x)/5 = 74, and read the x-intercept or the solved value.
Helpful for messy decimals, less so for multi-condition ordered-list questions.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You average the two group means as if the groups were the same size.
Or you forget to include the unknown in the count.
Or, when the mean must be an integer in a range, you stop before checking which candidate satisfies every constraint.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You average the two group means as if the groups were the same size.
